title: Tuples
description: A tuple is a list whose values are locked the moment you make it.

content.text: A list is built to be changed, but some values never should: the days of the week, a pair of map coordinates. A **tuple** is a sealed box for values like that. You can look through the clear lid and read what's inside, but you cannot add, remove or swap anything once it is sealed.

content.title: Reading a tuple works just like reading a list

content.value:
months = ("January", "February", "March")

print(months[0])
print(months[-1])
print(len(months))

for month in months:
    print(month)

content.question: What does this print?
content.explain: `-1` counts back from the end, just like a list. The last item is `30`.

items: The one thing you cannot do is **change** a tuple.
There is no `.append()` on a tuple.
Assigning to an index stops the program with a `TypeError`.

content.value: Switch the lab below over to tuple and try the buttons to see Python refuse.

items.title: Tuple: TypeError
items.text: Python refuses: a tuple cannot be changed after it is made.

content.title: Change a list vs change a tuple
content.caption: That refusal is the feature, not a limitation. If a value is never meant to move, a tuple makes moving it by accident impossible. Anyone reading your code can see at a glance that it is fixed.

content.question: What happens when this runs?
content.explain: Tuples have no `.append()`. Python refuses to change a tuple, so the program stops with an error before reaching `print`.

content.title: Ask: will it grow, shrink or change? Yes: list. No: tuple.

items.title: A tuple
items.text: Prints `(5,)`. The trailing comma makes it a tuple.

items.title: Just a number
items.text: Prints `5`. Without the comma, the brackets just wrap a number.

content.title: The one item tuple trap
content.caption: A one item tuple needs a trailing comma: `(5,)`. This one catches almost everybody once.

content.question: Which should be a tuple?
options: The red, green and blue numbers of a colour
High scores that grow over time
content.explain: A colour's three numbers never change while the program runs. The others all grow or change, so they should be lists.

quiz.question: Which brackets make a tuple?
quiz.explain: Tuples use parentheses. Square brackets make lists and curly brackets make dictionaries.

quiz.question: What happens when you run  colors = ("red", "blue")  then  colors.append("green")?
options: The tuple gains a third item
Python raises an error, because a tuple cannot be changed
The tuple turns into a list
quiz.explain: A tuple has no .append() at all, so Python stops with an AttributeError. That protection is the whole reason to pick a tuple.

quiz.question: Which of these is the better job for a tuple?
options: A shopping list you keep adding to
The fixed pair of numbers giving a treasure's location
The names of players who have joined a game so far
A queue of jobs waiting to be done
quiz.explain: The other three all grow or shrink while the program runs, so they need lists. A fixed location never changes, so locking it is helpful.
